name: Bard
summary: Whether scholar, skald, or scoundrel, a bard weaves magic through words and music to inspire allies, demoralize foes, manipulate minds, create illusions, and even heal wounds. The bard is a master of song, speech, and the magic they contain.
multiclassRequirement: You must have a Charisma score of 13 or higher in order to multiclass in or out of this class.

hitPoints.Hit Points at Higher Levels: 1d8 (or 5) + your Constitution modifier per bard level after 1st

proficiencies.Weapons: Simple weapons, hand crossbows, longswords, rapiers, shortswords
proficiencies.Tools: Three musical instruments of your choice

spellcastingTable.title: You must have a Charisma score of 13 or higher in order to multiclass in or out of this class.
rows: Jack of All Trades, Song of Rest (d6), Magical Inspiration (Optional)

spellcastingNotes: You have learned to untangle and reshape the fabric of reality in harmony with your wishes and music. Your spells are part of your vast repertoire, magic that you can tune to different situations.
You know two cantrips of your choice from the bard spell list. You learn additional bard cantrips of your choice at higher levels, as shown in the Cantrips Known column of the Bard table.

The Bard table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your bard spells of 1st level and higher. To cast one of these spells, you must expend a slot of the spell's level or higher. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a long rest. For example, if you know the 1st-level spell Cure Wounds and have a 1st-level and a 2nd-level spell slot available, you can cast Cure Wounds using either slot.
You know four 1st-level spells of your choice from the bard spell list.

The Spells Known column of the Bard table shows when you learn more bard spells of your choice. Each of these spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots, as shown on the table. For instance, when you reach 3rd level in this class, you can learn one new spell of 1st or 2nd level.

Additionally, when you gain a level in this class, you can choose one of the bard spells you know and replace it with another spell from the bard spell list, which also must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

Charisma is your spellcasting ability for your bard spells. Your magic comes from the heart and soul you pour into the performance of your music or oration. You use your Charisma whenever a spell refers to your spellcasting ability. In addition, you use your Charisma modifier when setting the saving throw DC for a bard spell you cast and when making an attack roll with one.
Spell save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier

classFeatures.name: Bardic Inspiration
keyFacts: Uses a bonus action.
Choose one creature other than yourself within 60 feet who can hear you.
The target adds the die to one ability check, attack roll, or saving throw.
Uses refresh on a long rest.
classFeatures.currentValueTemplate: Inspiration die scales by bard level
classFeatures.summary: You can inspire others through stirring words or music. To do so, you use a bonus action on your turn to choose one creature other than yourself within 60 feet of you who can hear you. That creature gains one Bardic Inspiration die, a d6. Once within the next 10 minutes, the creature can roll the die and add the number rolled to one ability check, attack roll, or saving throw it makes. The creature can wait until after it rolls the d20 before deciding to use the Bardic Inspiration die, but must decide before the DM says whether the roll succeeds or fails. Once the Bardic Inspiration die is rolled, it is lost. A creature can have only one Bardic Inspiration die at a time. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (a minimum of once). You regain any expended uses when you finish a long rest. Your Bardic Inspiration die changes when you reach certain levels in this class. The die becomes a d8 at 5th level, a d10 at 10th level, and a d12 at 15th level.

classFeatures.name: Jack of All Trades
keyFacts: Applies to ability checks that do not already include your proficiency bonus.
Adds half your proficiency bonus, rounded down.
Improves automatically as your proficiency bonus increases.

milestones.label: Add half proficiency to eligible ability checks

classFeatures.summary: Starting at 2nd level, you can add half your proficiency bonus, rounded down, to any ability check you make that doesn't already include your proficiency bonus.

classFeatures.name: Song of Rest
keyFacts: Triggers at the end of a short rest.
Applies when an ally spends one or more Hit Dice.
Adds extra healing to each resting creature who can hear the performance.
classFeatures.currentValueTemplate: Extra healing die scales by bard level
classFeatures.summary: Beginning at 2nd level, you can use soothing music or oration to help revitalize your wounded allies during a short rest. If you or any friendly creatures who can hear your performance regain hit points at the end of the short rest by spending one or more Hit Dice, each of those creatures regains an extra 1d6 hit points. The extra Hit Points increase when you reach certain levels in this class: to 1d8 at 9th level, to 1d10 at 13th level, and to 1d12 at 17th level.

classFeatures.name: Magical Inspiration (Optional)
keyFacts: Optional 2nd-level bard feature.
A creature can spend your Bardic Inspiration on a healing or damage spell.
The inspiration die is added to one affected target's healing or damage.
classFeatures.summary: At 2nd level, if a creature has a Bardic Inspiration die from you and casts a spell that restores hit points or deals damage, the creature can roll that die and choose a target affected by the spell. Add the number rolled as a bonus to the hit points regained or the damage dealt. The Bardic Inspiration die is then lost.

classFeatures.name: Expertise
keyFacts: Choose two of your skill proficiencies at 3rd level.
Your proficiency bonus is doubled for checks using those skills.
Choose two more skill proficiencies at 10th level.
classFeatures.summary: At 3rd level, choose two of your skill proficiencies. Your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make that uses either of the chosen proficiencies. At 10th level, you can choose another two skill proficiencies to gain this benefit.

classFeatures.name: Ability Score Improvement
keyFacts: Earn an ASI choice at specific bard levels.
Increase one ability by 2 or two abilities by 1.
Can also trigger Bardic Versatility if you use that optional rule.
classFeatures.summary: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

classFeatures.name: Bardic Versatility (Optional)
keyFacts: Optional feature tied to ASI levels.
Replace one Expertise skill with another eligible skill.
Or replace one bard cantrip with another bard cantrip.
classFeatures.summary: Whenever you reach a level in this class that grants the Ability Score Improvement feature, you can do one of the following, representing a change in focus as you use your skills and magic: Replace one of the skills you chose for the Expertise feature with one of your other skill proficiencies that isn't benefiting from Expertise. Replace one cantrip you learned from this class's Spellcasting feature with another cantrip from the bard spell list.

classFeatures.name: Font of Inspiration
keyFacts: Bardic Inspiration uses refresh on short rests as well as long rests.
Makes inspiration easier to spend between encounters.
Turns Bardic Inspiration into a regular party-facing resource.

milestones.label: Bardic Inspiration refreshes on short or long rest

classFeatures.summary: Beginning when you reach 5th level, you regain all of your expended uses of Bardic Inspiration when you finish a short or long rest.

classFeatures.name: Countercharm
keyFacts: Uses an action to start a performance.
You and nearby allies gain advantage against frightened and charmed.
Affects friendly creatures within 30 feet who can hear you.
classFeatures.summary: At 6th level, you gain the ability to use musical notes or words of power to disrupt mind-influencing effects. As an action, you can start a performance that lasts until the end of your next turn. During that time, you and any friendly creatures within 30 feet of you have advantage on saving throws against being frightened or charmed. A creature must be able to hear you to gain this benefit. The performance ends early if you are incapacitated or silenced or if you voluntarily end it (no action required).

classFeatures.name: Magical Secrets
keyFacts: Choose spells from any class list.
Chosen spells count as bard spells for you.
Spells must be a level you can cast, or cantrips.
classFeatures.summary: By 10th level, you have plundered magical knowledge from a wide spectrum of disciplines. Choose two spells from any classes, including this one. A spell you choose must be of a level you can cast, as shown on the Bard table, or a cantrip. The chosen spells count as bard spells for you and are included in the number in the Spells Known column of the Bard table. You learn two additional spells from any classes at 14th level and again at 18th level.

classFeatures.name: Superior Inspiration
keyFacts: Triggers when you roll initiative.
Only applies if you have no Bardic Inspiration uses left.
Restores one Bardic Inspiration use.

milestones.label: Regain 1 inspiration when initiative starts and you have none

classFeatures.summary: At 20th level, when you roll initiative and have no uses of Bardic Inspiration left, you regain one use.
